name: mathrsi-meta-evolve

name: mathrsi-prepare

name: mathrsi-prove

name: mathrsi-research
description: 端到端数学研究主工作流，实际串联问题准备与文献、求解路线对抗迭代、证明推进、完整装配验证和可复现交付。组合本仓MathRSI与ARIS技能及领域插件，遇新障碍定向回文献/路线，复用wiki与证据，按需Lean。

name: mathrsi-route-loop
description: 执行ARIS auto-review-loop的数学路线适配，准备具体方法，经真实research-review、持续reviewer memory、实际推导或探针、修复复核与逐轮恢复，交付可执行求解路线和未证义务。用于选择或改造证明方法及重判卡住的路线；完整证明验收交给mathrsi-verify。

name: mathrsi-specify

name: mathrsi-survey

name: mathrsi-verify

description: 麦当劳中国官方 MCP 智能助手。当用户提到麦当劳、金拱门、麦乐送、到店取餐、麦咖啡、麦麦省、优惠券、领券、活动日历、麦当劳活动、品牌联名、联名款、联名周边、限定、IP合作、积分、麦麦商城、抽奖、点餐、下单、比价、怎么点最划算、拼单、群点、聚餐点餐、办公室下午茶、夜宵拼单、多人点餐、分摊等，优先使用本 skill。四大能力：①获取最新活动推送（查询当月营销活动日历并摘要推送）；②联名关注推送（盯联名/限定活动：按 config/keywords.json 中的关键词筛选活动并推送，默认关键词「联名」+ 同义词扩展，支持对话增删关键词）；③最优惠点餐（门店→菜单→领券→算价的全链路比价，输出应付金额最低的组合）；④多人群点聚合（聚餐拼单：代录全员餐品→满减凑单→券归属→公共费用分摊（配送费+打包费）→自动生成每人账单，组织者单账户统一结算）。**点餐入口会先主动询问「单人还是多人拼单」，命中多人即转入④，无需用户自己提出。**另含社交媒体场景六项：隐藏吃法一键还原（文案/截图解析→单品映射→特调/备注→下单）、穷鬼套餐凑单演算、周边联名抢货雷达（按需扫店+麦金卡随单购优化；无实时库存接口）、参数化营养搭配（热量/蛋白/控糖约束）、晒单卡片生成、天气与场景感应推送。

name: mcd-desktop-pet

description: 麦当劳点餐（mcd-mcp）的专用下单流程：自动排查并去除酸黄瓜，同时自动定位门店、领取优惠券、盘活积分并对多套方案比价，做到不吃酸瓜且价格最优。当用户要在麦当劳下单、点汉堡或套餐、查询餐品成分、问优惠券/积分怎么用，或提到"不要酸黄瓜 / 不加酸瓜 / 去酸黄瓜 / 忌口酸瓜"时使用。即使用户没提酸黄瓜，只要走麦当劳下单，也必须执行本 skill 的酸瓜检查。

Nothing is deleted. Use when the user says "archive tasks", "clean up done tasks", "move done to history", or runs `/mdn-archive`.

name: mdn-daily
description: Meridian daily review skill. Read-only. Surfaces what needs the human today across all active projects: tasks in review (the agent finished and is waiting for you), your own tasks in backlog or in progress, and blocked tasks. Use when the user says "what do I need to do today", "show my tasks", "what is waiting for my review", "daily meridian", or runs `/mdn-daily`.

name: mdn-done
description: Meridian review-closing skill. The human accepts a task that is in review, marking it done with an optional review note, or sends it back to in-progress with a reason. Use when the user says "mark as done", "accept this task", "close the task", "I reviewed it", "reopen the task", or runs `/mdn-done`.

name: mdn-init
description: Meridian project initializer. On first run, detects missing config and asks the user for their Obsidian vault path, writing it to ~/.config/meridian/config.md. Then creates a new Meridian project (one project.md file) inside the vault's `meridian/` directory and fills its one-line description from the repository context. Also runs in auto mode when another Meridian command finds the project not initialized. Use when the user says "create a new Meridian project", "init a project", "start a new project in Meridian", or runs `/mdn-init name:<slug>`.

name: mdn-md
description: Read MDN docs from mdn/content source markdown instead of fetching rendered pages. Use for any task that needs MDN articles.

name: mdn-run
description: Meridian execution skill and the single trigger of the ODD flow. Records a task in the Meridian project note before work starts, runs the work through the gentle-ai ODD workflow in the main thread, then completes the Run and Trace metadata from git/gh and moves the task to review. Accepts a free-text description, `task:<slug>` to run or resume an existing task, or `next` for the first agent backlog task. Use when the user says "run this", "implement this and track it", "run the next task", "resume the task", "retoma la feature", or runs `/mdn-run`.

name: mdn-status
description: Meridian status skill. Read-only. Prints task counts by status and owner for every active project plus a total, and flags in-progress tasks whose run started more than 24 hours ago as possibly stale. Use when the user says "show project status", "what's the state of my projects", or runs `/mdn-status`.

name: melfina-write-shared

name: memex-wrap

name: memex-writing-plans
description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code

name: memex:brain:ask
description: Ask a natural-language question against the personal Brain. Routes through the Reference Librarian subagent which builds a query plan (FTS5 + optional vector), Python executes against ~/.memex/index.db, fetches full rows from target stores, and returns ranked citation-ready hits.

name: memex:brain:capture
description: Capture a free-form note or observation into the personal Brain (~/.memex/article.db.captures). Lighter than ingest — no source URL, no raw archive, but still routed through the Librarian subagent for classification and linking.

name: memex:brain:community-report
description: Generate a bottom-up structured report (title, summary, importance rating, findings) for one detected community in the GraphRAG knowledge graph. Option-B Task-tool dispatch — the Community Reporter subagent summarizes member documents (and rolled-up child-community reports) under a character budget; Python persists the report (+ embedding) to ~/.memex/index.db.community_reports. One LLM call per community.

name: memex:brain:graph-rebuild
description: Operator maintenance entry point for the GraphRAG knowledge layer — (re)build the lexical similarity graph over document text (key-free, no embedding provider required), detect hierarchical communities, then generate the missing community reports. Run after a batch of ingests, or whenever the Index has drifted from the derived graph/community/report artifacts.

name: memex:brain:ingest
description: Ingest an article or external source into the personal Brain (~/.memex/article.db). Routes through Archivist (preserves raw), Librarian subagent (classifies + assigns index_id, relations), and Memex Core (persists). Hash-based rerun safety — re-ingesting the same canonical content is a silent skip.

name: memex:brain:lint
description: Run a Data Steward audit over your Brain. Detects orphans (index entries without matching article/capture/synthesis rows), broken relations, and integrity drift. Read-only; reports findings; does not auto-fix.

name: memex:brain:synthesize
description: Produce a cross-document synthesis on a topic. Two subagent dispatches — Synthesizer reads sources + topic and produces prose; Librarian classifies the resulting synthesis. name: memex:codegraph:ingest
description: Ingest a graphify code-navigation graph.json into the SEPARATE code_graph.db store, keyed by repo identity (owner/repo). The extractor is external — run `graphify update <path> --no-cluster` first; memex only stores + queries (no tree-sitter/networkx imports, no LLM).

name: memex:codegraph:query
description: Query the code-navigation graph store (code_graph.db) for kaizen/atelier recon — where_is, callers, dependencies, neighbors, module_map. Bounded returns (locations + rows, NEVER file bodies; BFS capped by max_nodes as a token-budget analog), deterministic ordering, scoped by repo identity. Pure deterministic SQL; no LLM.

name: memex:core:create-store
description: Create a new Memex-managed SQLite store from a directory of SQL migration files. Use when a consumer (Atelier, Brain, custom) needs a fresh project- or domain-scoped store. Memex creates the file with WAL pragmas, installs the universal migrations table, applies each .sql file in lexical order, and registers the store in the global registry.

name: memex:core:delete
description: Delete a row by integer `id` PK from a registered Memex store. Returns true if a row was deleted, false otherwise. Document deletes should also notify the Librarian (deferred to Plan 2).

name: memex:core:get-agent
description: Fetch an agent's full profile (including markdown profile body) by agent_id. Used by the Librarian, Reference Librarian, and other Memex internal agents to read created_by profiles for context-aware decision-making.

name: memex:core:insert
description: Insert a row into a table of a registered Memex store. Use for non-document tables (lookup tables, configuration, agents, roles). For document rows that need to be indexed, use memex:index:write instead — that routes through the Librarian.

name: memex:core:list-stores
description: List every registered Memex store on this machine — name, absolute path, schema version, registration time.

name: memex:core:migrate
description: Apply additional SQL migration files to an existing Memex-managed store. Idempotent — already-applied migrations (tracked in the store's `migrations` table) are skipped. Use when a consumer's schema evolves and new .sql files need to be applied to an in-place store without recreating it.

name: memex:core:query
description: Run a SELECT query against any registered Memex store. Returns rows as a list of dicts. Use for read-only operations; for full-text or vector search, use memex:index:search instead.

name: memex:core:register-agent
description: Register a new agent in the global agents.db agents table. Every Memex write requires an agent_id; this is how agents (human or LLM, internal or consumer-provided) come into existence.

name: memex:core:register-role
description: Register a new role in the global agents.db roles table. Roles are universal (Memex-managed schema, multi-tenant rows). Consumers (Atelier, future plugins) call this on install to seed their own role taxonomies.

name: memex:core:update
description: Update a single row by integer `id` PK in a registered Memex store. Use for partial updates of non-document rows; document content updates should re-trigger indexing via memex:index:write.

name: memex:dba:checkpoint
description: Run a WAL checkpoint on a registered store. Mode defaults to PASSIVE.

name: memex:dba:integrity-check
description: Run PRAGMA integrity_check on a registered store. Returns 'ok' if clean, otherwise a string describing issues.

name: memex:dba:vacuum
description: Run VACUUM on a registered store to reclaim space and defragment. Should be run during maintenance windows, not under live load.

name: memex:embed:backfill
description: Re-encode every documents row with `embedding IS NULL` using the currently-configured provider. Idempotent — non-NULL rows are untouched. Use after first configuring an embedding API key, or after ingesting documents while no provider was set.

name: memex:embed:reembed
description: Re-encode EVERY documents row (NULL and non-NULL) using the currently-configured provider. Use after a deliberate provider or model change — old embeddings are dimensionally or semantically incomparable with new ones. Destructive — overwrites existing embeddings. Has a confirmation gate.

name: memex:index:archive

name: memex:index:search

name: memex:index:write

name: memex:steward:audit

name: memex:steward:audit-store

name: memex:steward:dashboard

Empty fleet_status is not permission to skip the protocol — it just means you're the first agent in thi…

Do not start the leader phase without first checking fleet_status; do not let followers free-claim leaves without a correlation tag — you will not be able to aggregate results. Skip this skill for single-a…

name: memfleet-fleet-status
description: Always use as the once-per-session opener and as the periodic dashboard refresh. Returns active intents, open subscriptions, episode counts, and conflict counts split by class. Triggered by: 'how busy is the fleet', 'are there open conflicts', 'is anyone working on this repo', pre-release coordination check, leader pre-flight before a coordinated wave, periodic ops dashboard. Do not skip this call before launching a multi-symbol refactor — high class-B/C counts mean the wave will collide. Do not use it as a per-symbol query; for that use get_node_state.

name: memfleet-node-state
description: Always use to read current coordination state for a symbol — recent episodes, active intents, dominant intent, conflict density, Y-doc thread. Triggered by: 'is anyone working on X', pre-edit reconnaissance, checking fleet activity on a symbol, reading another agent's recent work, debugging why a publish_intent returned a conflict. Do not grep the codebase to figure out 'who edited this last' — the broker has a precomputed O(1) rollup. Do not call get_node_state in a tight loop expecting push semantics; for streaming, use subscribe.

name: memfleet-publish-intent
description: Always use BEFORE modifying any symbol in a multi-agent session to register structural intent and surface blast radius + active conflicts. Triggered by: about to refactor / rename / delete / modify code, planning an edit, checking if another agent is working on the same area, pre-edit coordination, leader-driven multi-symbol waves. Do not edit first and publish after — the whole point is to surface conflicts BEFORE the wasted edit. Do not pass intent_kind as a flat string; it is a typed enum with a JSON-object shape.

name: memfleet-query-episodes

Triggered by: 'what changed this morning', 'who last touched the auth module', 'show me the conflict inbox', 'did anyone try X recently', polling for new fleet activity when no subscription is registered, post-incident retrospective. Do not use it for per-symbol activity (get_node_state is cheaper) or for fetching a single known episode (use get_episode). Polling with query_episodes is the FALLBACK when subscribe push is unavailable; in Phase-2, prefer subscribe.

name: memfleet-record-episode
description: Always use IMMEDIATELY AFTER an edit completes to record the structural episode, classify A/B/C conflict class, and update NodeState rollups for all touched + propagated nodes. Triggered by: finished writing code, about to commit, reporting edit completion to the fleet, multi-agent wave follower reporting back. Do not record multiple episodes for one semantic edit, do not pass a prose diff_summary, and do not delay the call until 'end of session' — every other agent reads stale rollups until you record.

name: memfleet-safe-edit
description: Always use as the end-to-end workflow around any edit in a multi-agent session — get_node_state → publish_intent → edit → record_episode → branch on conflict class. Triggered by: 'implement X', 'rename Y', 'add feature Z', 'apply this fix' when other agents may be active. Do not skip publish_intent because you 'know' the symbol is quiet, do not record_episode with a prose diff_summary instead of a structural one, and do not retry on Class C without reading the conflict report. This is the canonical fleet-safe edit loop.

name: memfleet-subscribe

Triggered by: long-running agent sessions (anything > one edit), follower role in a leader-orchestrated wave, watching a specific module for fleet activity, ops dashboards. Do not register a subscription for a single one-shot edit (use get_node_state and skip the channel). Phase-1 push is stub — verify with a kickoff probe before relying on push semantics.

description: Use when comparing metagenomic binning tools on real short-read (human gut, dog gut, ocean, soil) or long-read (human gut, sheep gut, activated sludge) projects to quantify gains in high-quality bin reconstruction.

name: metagenomic-binning-and-scaffold-clustering
description: Use when a hybrid metagenome assembly (Illumina paired-end plus ONT/PacBio long reads or mate pairs) must be partitioned into species-specific scaffold clusters, or when near-complete genomes and biologically important elements must be detected per bin.

name: metagenomic-biomarker-visualization
description: Use when you have LEfSe biomarker results and a MetaPhlAn (or HUMAnN) abundance profile and need a publication-quality circular cladogram highlighting discriminatory taxa with metadata overlays.

name: metagenomic-catalogue-construction
description: Use when short-read metagenomic (FASTQ.GZ) data from mixed microbial communities must be mined for novel insertion sequences and consolidated into a non-redundant FASTA catalogue for downstream annotation or genome querying.

name: metagenomic-cds-dereplication
description: Use when building a body-site non-redundant gene catalog from a large set of predicted CDSs (nucleotide FASTA) and redundant near-identical sequences across metagenomes must be collapsed into cluster representatives for downstream annotation and read mapping.

name: metagenomic-clade-association-testing
description: Use when QCed shotgun metagenomic FASTQ data from case and control cohorts are available and per-clade disease association statistics (p-values/FDR) are needed via phylogenetic profiling.

name: metagenomic-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing taxonomic classification accuracy (sensitivity/precision) of metagenomic classifiers on simulated read sets with known origins, e.g. Kraken vs BLAST-based or k-mer-based classifiers.

name: metagenomic-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how a taxonomic classifier behaves on reads from species missing from its database, i.e. when quantifying false positives caused by similarity to the closest available relative rather than true species presence.

name: metagenomic-classifier-database-building
description: Use when building a custom Kraken taxonomy database from a set of reference genomes (e.g. NCBI RefSeq complete microbial genomes) so every k-mer maps to an LCA taxonomic label.

name: metagenomic-composition-estimation
description: Use when long-read (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) metagenomic FASTQ reads must be assigned per-read to taxa and converted into strain- or species-level sample composition estimates against a reference database such as miniSeq+H/RefSeq.

name: metagenomic-consensus-genome-assembly
description: Use when nanopore FASTQ/FAST5/POD5 sample folders must be turned into per-sample viral consensus genomes with taxonomic labels (KMA → assembly → Kraken2 → Krona) as part of the VirDetector pipeline.

name: metagenomic-contamination-assessment
description: Use when validating that a custom marker-gene or reference database is specific to its target kingdom by measuring how many of its sequences align against a large out-group reference catalog (e.g., fungal markers vs. a bacterial gut genome catalog).

name: metagenomic-contig-binning
description: Use when starting from a metagenomic de Bruijn-graph assembly (FASTA contigs >=500 bp) plus the trimmed reads, and the goal is a bin-quality table of completeness and strain heterogeneity per bin.

name: metagenomic-contig-binning
description: Use when starting from paired-end metagenomic shotgun reads (e.g. FASTQ) and non-redundant MAG sets are needed as input for downstream MAG taxonomy classification, especially for benchmarking classifiers.

name: metagenomic-contig-classification
description: Use when a metagenomic or plasmidome assembly (FASTA contigs/scaffolds) needs plasmid-vs-chromosome assignment with initial phylum-level taxonomy, and kmer-signature classification without prior knowledge of sample composition is appropriate.

name: metagenomic-contig-clustering-by-organism
description: Use when metagenomic shotgun reads/contigs must be grouped by organism of origin before downstream per-group model fitting, e.g. to gate retraining of gene prediction IMMs within each cluster.

name: metagenomic-contig-colinearity-analysis
description: Use when a post-assembly contig set (e.g., MergedContigs.fasta from MeGAMerge) contains very large contigs (hundreds of kb) whose contiguity must be confirmed by whole-contig colinear alignment to a single reference genome, such as Supplementary Figures S4-S5 validation.

name: metagenomic-contig-depth-estimation
description: Use when you have assembled metagenomic contigs plus per-sample short-read FASTQs and need per-contig mean sequencing depths across samples to feed co-abundance-based binning (e.g., MetaBAT2) or to estimate MAG abundances.

name: metagenomic-contig-dereplication
description: Use when multiple assembled metagenome contig FASTA files (e.g. from SOAPdenovo, CLC Bio, Velvet, Newbler) must be pooled and deduplicated prior to OLC-based merging, and exact duplicates, reverse complements, or subsequences must be eliminated first.

name: metagenomic-contig-extension
description: Use when metaSPAdes or another de novo assembler has produced viral metagenomic seed contigs of only a few kb and the goal is to lengthen them with paired or unpaired FASTQ reads while checking accuracy against NCBI viral reference sequences.

name: metagenomic-contig-set-merging
description: Use when you have multiple FASTA files of assembled contigs from different assemblers (e.g., Velvet, SOAPdenovo, IDBA, Ray, CLC Bio) or related metagenome samples and want a single improved, more contiguous merged contig set.

name: metagenomic-contig-taxonomy-annotation
description: Use when you need to classify assembled metagenomic contigs as putative viral sequences and need a reproducible confidence label based on agreement across multiple detection tools rather than a single-tool call.

name: metagenomic-count-filtering
description: Use when a mapped gene frequency count table from a mapping-based metagenomic pipeline is sparse and compositional and must be filtered, length-corrected and CSS-normalized before taxonomic or functional (KO/EC/reaction) profiling.

name: metagenomic-count-normalization
description: Use when the input is a sparse, high-throughput marker-gene (OTU/species/taxon) count matrix with two or more sample groups, and per-feature differential abundance statistics must account for both normalization and under-sampling of microbial communities.

name: metagenomic-database-construction
description: Use when constructing a k-mer/minhash classification database from large multi-kingdom reference genome collections where full-database build exceeds workstation memory, or when benchmarking build time and peak RAM across partition/executor counts.

name: metagenomic-de-novo-assembly
description: Use when metagenomic Illumina (or 454) reads are available, multiple de novo assemblies (e.g. different kmer values or assemblers) have been generated, and improved contiguity (larger contigs, more genes) is needed beyond any single assembler run.

name: metagenomic-de-novo-assembly
description: Use when raw or preprocessed paired-end metagenome FASTQ reads must be assembled into contigs de novo as the first step toward building or reproducing a gene catalog such as VIRGO, and assembly statistics are the deliverable.

name: metagenomic-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when comparing metagenomic abundance profiles (taxon/gene/KO/EC/reaction tables) across phenotype groups (e.g. healthy vs adenoma vs carcinoma) to find significantly changed biomarker features while correcting compositional bias.

name: metagenomic-distance-behavior-validation
description: Use when you need to reproduce, reimplement, or validate scalable all-vs-all metagenome distance computation from k-mer frequency vectors, or sanity-check that a distance implementation yields near-zero self-distance.

name: metagenomic-fastq-accession-handling
description: Use when reproducing a k-mer abundance indexing/AMQ benchmark that requires concrete public metagenomic FASTQ runs — one dataset to build the index and an independent query dataset for FPR measurement.

name: metagenomic-fecal-source-tracking
description: Use when gzipped FASTQ shotgun metagenomes from water samples must be attributed to specific fecal source categories and apportioned by cell fraction, without sequencing the potential sources themselves.

name: metagenomic-flanking-region-extraction
description: Use when short-read metagenomic FASTQ data must yield the genomic context (flanking regions) around ARGs or other target genes, and full de novo assembly would be computationally prohibitive.

name: metagenomic-functional-annotation
description: Use when you have shotgun metagenomics sequencing data (e.g. FASTQ from fecal samples) and need functional pathway enrichment comparisons between groups rather than only taxonomic composition.

name: metagenomic-functional-annotation-level-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing between gene-level and functional-level (KO/EC/reaction) differential analysis of mapped metagenomic count data, when you have per-level significance ratios from a case-control dataset such as CAMAMED's colorectal adenoma/carcinoma (CAMAMED) run.

name: metagenomic-functional-annotation-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when installing MetaLAFFA or customizing its pipeline operation — choosing steps, per-step parameters, cluster submission settings, or reference databases (UniRef90, KEGG mappings, host decoys) — prior to annotating shotgun metagenomic FASTQ data.

name: metagenomic-functional-pathway-profiling
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic case-control data (e.g. SCZ n=344, T2D n=171) require pathway-level enrichment testing and integration with host GWAS summary statistics to evaluate pathway overlap.

name: metagenomic-functional-profiling
description: Use when metagenomic reads have already been mapped to a non-redundant gene catalog yielding per-sample gene frequencies, and the goal is to extend these into KO, EC number and reaction annotations with per-sample functional frequencies.

name: metagenomic-gene-catalogue-processing
description: Use when a metagenomic analysis needs gene clusters grouped by genomic adjacency (synteny) to associate functional content and shared pathways with MAG clusters or subspecies clades.

name: metagenomic-gene-cluster-functional-summarization
description: Use when you have MAGinator synteny_clusters.tab output plus a non-redundant gene catalogue and need to attach KEGG module assignments per synteny cluster and measure functional coherence.

name: metagenomic-gene-cluster-mining
description: Use when starting from microbial genome assemblies and needing predicted MGCs/BGCs reduced to representative GCFs as mapping targets for metagenomic or metatranscriptomic abundance analysis.

name: metagenomic-gene-count-matrix-curation
description: Use when profiling de novo MAG clusters from shotgun metagenomics requires cluster-specific signature genes: you have a gene read-count matrix (small_gene_count_matrix.tsv) and MAG cluster assignments (metagenomicspecies.tab) and need abundance-grade gene sets.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when comparing merged (MeGAMerge) vs individual metagenomic assemblies by predicted gene counts and coding density, or when annotating contigs >=2 kb without a reference genome.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic reads or scaftigs (FASTA) lack gene annotations and gene coordinates are required as input for operon/proximon prediction (e.g. MetaRon 'ago' or 'op' mode).

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when input is unassembled metagenomic DNA reads (e.g. Sanger, 454, or Illumina shotgun reads) and the goal is nucleotide-level gene prediction with sensitivity/precision scoring against known gene coordinates.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when you have assembled genome FASTA files (MAGs, fungal genomes, viral genomes/vOTUs) and need translated protein-coding gene sequences as input for downstream gene clustering, annotation or gene catalogue construction.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when input is a metagenome assembly FASTA (human microbiome contigs) needing gene prediction in GTF format, and near-complete-genome accuracy is required for short contigs without genomic context.

name: metagenomic-gene-to-ortholog-mapping
description: Use when you have a gene-level (e.g. UniRef90-based, length-normalized) abundance table and a gene-to-KO mapping file, and need a KO-level functional profile per sample.

name: metagenomic-genome-assembly
description: Use when processing shotgun viral metagenomic FASTQ reads in ViroProfiler and you need per-sample assembled contigs plus a single species-level non-redundant contig library (nrclib.fasta) for downstream annotation, taxonomy assignment, and analysis.

name: metagenomic-genome-dereplication
description: Use when a genome set assembled/binned from metagenomes will be used as a concatenated mapping reference or for cross-tool strain-sharing benchmarks, and redundant near-identical genomes (e.g. >98% ANI) must be collapsed first.

name: metagenomic-genome-size-estimation
description: Use when metagenomic read-mapping results (per-genome sequence depth X from CoverM against source-associated genome databases) must be normalized to genome equivalents to express source signal as approximate cell fractions.

name: metagenomic-hic-binning-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing viral binning tools on metagenomic Hi-C datasets (shotgun + Hi-C FASTQ pairs from SRA/ENA) and evaluating recovered vMAGs by completeness categories.

name: metagenomic-hic-multi-dataset-quality-benchmarking
description: Use when you have cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads from several metagenomic Hi-C datasets and need a reference-free, quantitative measure of ligation/library quality comparable across datasets.

name: metagenomic-hit-summarization
description: Use when you have filtered read-to-gene DIAMOND alignment hits ( e-value per read) from shotgun metagenomic data and need to compute per-gene abundance counts, including fractional assignment of multi-mapping reads.

name: metagenomic-import
description: Import WGS/metagenomic Bracken reports into a complete phyloseq object (tax, otu, sam, tree) with host cleanup. Use when importing Bracken/Kraken reports, building WGS phyloseq, or when the user mentions metagenomic-import.

name: metagenomic-is-candidate-screening
description: Use when paired-end short-read metagenomic reads have already been screened for inverted repeats by pal-MEM (LCoord/RCoord annotated FASTA) and sample assemblies exist, and you need proximity-filtered candidate ITR reads.

name: metagenomic-krona-chart
description: Analyze data with `metagenomic-krona-chart` using a reproducible workflow, explicit validation, and structured outputs for review-ready interpretation.

name: metagenomic-marker-consensus-sequencing
description: Use when MetaPhlAn 4 profiles detect a target species (including taxonomically unidentified SGBs) across many shotgun metagenomes and you need a strain phylogeny or strain-sharing/transmission analysis from marker alignments.

name: metagenomic-marker-database-construction
description: Use when building or reproducing a reference marker-gene database from a large genome catalog (isolates plus MAGs), e.g. deriving SGBs and unique markers underlying MetaPhlAn 4-style taxonomic profiling.

name: metagenomic-metadata-regression-modeling
description: Use when you have a microbial feature abundance table (taxonomic or functional profiles) plus sample metadata (e.g. geography, health status, extraction method) and need significant feature–variable associations from multivariable linear models.

name: metagenomic-mock-data-simulation
description: Use when a reproducible mock compositional abundance table (with matched control/disease phenotype data) is needed to test or benchmark metagenomic feature-enrichment or causality-inference methods such as VTwins.

name: metagenomic-multi-sample-contig-binning
description: Use when you have metagenomic short-read samples from multiple environments and want to bin contigs across samples jointly (multi-sample mode), comparing or replacing single-sample binners like VAMB.

name: metagenomic-pipeline-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify wall-clock time, peak memory footprint, and CPU-hour usage of a Snakemake-based metagenomic pipeline (e.g. ARGprofiler with fastp, KMA, ARGextender, SPAdes, Mash rules) under its final parameter settings.

name: metagenomic-preprocessing
description: Use when raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQs must be cleaned before functional annotation — removing human/host reads, PCR or optical duplicates, and low-quality or too-short reads prior to gene mapping.

name: metagenomic-preprocessing-pipeline
description: Use when raw metagenomic samples arrive as SRA archives and must be converted to FASTQ/FASTA, quality-checked, and characterized with per-sample sequence statistics before taxonomic/functional mapping.

name: metagenomic-profiler-versus-ground-truth-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking a taxonomic profiler against a known ground truth (e.g. CAMI marmgCAMI2_short_read_sample_0) and you need clade-level presence/absence discordance beyond F1 or UniFrac scores.

name: metagenomic-protein-assembly
description: Use when the goal is to maximize protein sequence recovery from complex metagenomic or metatranscriptomic short-read data (paired-end FASTQ or single-end FASTA/FASTQ) by assembling directly at the protein level.

name: metagenomic-protein-database-construction
description: Use when analyzing metaproteomics tandem MS/MS spectra against metagenome-derived protein databases (metapeptide or non-redundant environmental FASTA), or when benchmarking database search vs de novo peptide-detection counts.

name: metagenomic-protein-sequence-screening
description: Use when you need to identify and type-classify proteins (e.g. DsrA/DsrB and paralogous families) in thousands of (meta)genomic protein sequences in FASTA format, at scale, without phylogenetic reconstruction.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g., the 30-sample BIO-ML set from PRJNA544527 or a 121-sample H. pylori eradication cohort) must be mapped to a reference database to generate per-sample BAMs for downstream variant detection.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment
description: Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads must be mapped to a combined microbiome reference FASTA while preserving junction pairs mapping across different references, as the first stage of LEMON's HGT detection pipeline.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-gene-catalog
description: Use when you have QC'd shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads and a non-redundant gene catalog (e.g., the IGC catalog), and you need per-sample gene frequencies as input to compositional differential-abundance analysis.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-genome-databases
description: Use when assigning shotgun metagenomic reads from water or mesocosm samples (e.g. FASTQ reads from PRJNA1161616) to individual genomes in a source-associated database to quantify per-genome and per-source-category signal.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-operons
description: Use when you have predicted operon sequences from metagenomic shotgun samples and raw paired-end reads, and need per-sample pathway/KO abundances to compare disease versus control groups.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-viral-scaffolds
description: Use when predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., from VIBRANT or VirSorter) must be binned from metagenomes and per-sample coverage tables are needed as input to vRhyme's coverage variance / effect-size binning network.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying high-throughput sequencing reads (Illumina FASTQ, single- or paired-end) from metagenomic whole-genome sequencing to NCBI taxa, especially when reference genomes are incomplete or distant strains must still be classified.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying shotgun FASTQ/FASTA reads from complex biological samples (e.g., calibrator sausage mixtures) against large reference genome collections to detect ingredient/species composition and estimate abundances with low false-positive rates.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying paired-end metagenomic reads (e.g. simulated setA2/setB2 or HMP metagenome SRR1804065) against a reference genome FASTA in alignment-free fashion, computing sensitivity/precision/F1/specificity.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying fastq/fasta metagenomic reads at species or genus rank, especially gut microbiome reads from uncultured MAGs where k-mer/LCA tools miss species absent from reference databases.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when assigning taxonomic labels to large sets of metagenomic reads (FASTQ/FASTA from SRA accessions such as SRS019120, SRS014468, SRS015055, or Mason-simulated reads), or when benchmarking classifier speed and accuracy against Megablast or MetaPhlAn.

name: metagenomic-read-classification-kraken2
description: Reference for applying Kraken 2 to classify 16S amplicon reads from mock community samples at species/genus level and comparing its accuracy against 16S-specific pipelines over matched reference libraries.

name: metagenomic-read-clustering
description: Use when metagenomic Illumina short reads must be split into strain/species-coherent read groups before per-cluster assembly, e.g. as the preprocessing step of an overlap-layout-consensus strain-aware assembly pipeline.

name: metagenomic-read-coordinate-processing
description: Use when scanning metagenomic FASTA reads with pal-MEM for inverted terminal repeats and you need to encode read coordinates in two-bit space, apply edge-boundary conditions, or exclude MEMs near read ends that arise from amplification artifacts.

name: metagenomic-read-counting-per-taxon
description: Use when you already have per-read taxonomic assignments from a MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark query run and need organism-level read counts and abundance percentages at a chosen rank such as species.

name: metagenomic-read-decontamination
description: Use when untargeted Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads from clinical or animal samples contain host (e.g. human, mouse, mastomys), reagent, or bacterial contamination that must be removed before viral de novo assembly.

name: metagenomic-read-digital-normalization
description: Use when raw paired-end virome FASTQ reads (e.g. SRA runs like SRR3458562 or SRR9875293) feed into VirMAP's mapping assembly, pileup rebuilding, or DIAMOND/BBMap alignment and read depth is uneven or redundant.

name: metagenomic-read-gene-annotation
description: Use when per-sample DIAMOND tabular hits against a gene catalog (e.g. UniRef90) need -e-value refinement and fractional gene counting to produce gene/orthology abundances from shotgun metagenomic FASTQs.

name: metagenomic-read-length-and-n-trimming
description: Use when raw or primer-trimmed amplicon FASTQ reads (454 or Illumina) show deteriorating 3'-end quality or embedded Ns and must be trimmed and length-filtered before dereplication and OTU clustering.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping
description: Use when metagenomic paired-end FASTQ reads need to be mapped to a multi-genome reference .fasta to quantify genome detection, coverage, microdiversity, or strain sharing (e.g., ZymoBIOMICS mock-community benchmarking).

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-abundance-profiling
description: Use when you have predicted MGC/BGC regions from antiSMASH/gutSMASH genomes plus shotgun metagenomic or metatranscriptomic reads (e.g., SRA accessions) and need RPKM abundance profiles and phenotype-differential cluster statistics.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-and-counting
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic reads (FASTQ) must be quantified against de novo MAG clusters or signature gene sets to estimate organism/subspecies abundances per sample, e.g. tracking B. infantis and B. longum across the COPSAC2010 and CHILD infant cohorts.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-quantification
description: Use when short-read shotgun metagenomes (FASTQ) must be converted from mapped-read counts into genome-equivalent relative abundances (cell fractions) against a source-associated genome database for source tracking.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-to-contigs
description: Use when you need to judge assembly quality by read support: you have assembled contig FASTA files (individual or merged) and matching trimmed reads, and want per-contig base-coverage percentages.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-to-gene-catalog
description: Use when you need to profile the taxonomic and/or functional composition of vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic FASTQ samples against the VIRGO gene catalog instead of assembling reads de novo.

name: metagenomic-read-pair-filtering
description: Use when metagenomic reads have been mapped to representative sub-species genomes (e.g. concatenated .fasta) and per-scaffold or per-genome coverage, clonality, nucleotide diversity, or SNV calls must be computed without contamination from falsely mapped read pairs.

name: metagenomic-read-pooling-and-spike-in-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a targeted assembly or annotation pipeline (e.g. CasCollect) against a complete metagenome assembly, and a simulated community with known CRISPR/Cas content and background host contamination is needed from raw FASTQ reads.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-control
description: Use when raw metagenomic sequencing FASTQ files must be converted into clean, host-free reads before taxonomic or functional profiling, or when reproducing the Liu 2020 metagenomic pipeline.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-control
description: Use when raw paired-end or single-end Illumina metagenomic FASTQ/fastq.gz reads must be adapter-trimmed and quality-trimmed before SSU rRNA read extraction or any 16S/18S-based taxonomic classification.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-control
description: Use when raw vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic fastq reads must be cleaned (human/rRNA removal) and mapped to a reference gene catalog such as VIRGO before taxonomic or functional profiling.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-filtering
description: Use when quality-controlling shotgun metagenomic FASTQs as part of an end-to-end functional annotation pipeline, after host and duplicate read filtering and before mapping reads to a gene database.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g. SRA accession SRR606249, 2 x 100 bp) must be cleaned prior to meta-assembly with metaSPAdes or MegaHIT.

name: metagenomic-read-query-execution
description: Use when benchmarking fimpera-style amplified s-mer querying of a counting Bloom filter on metagenomic FASTQ reads, specifically to verify that query time stays flat or slightly decreases as z increases.

name: metagenomic-read-recruitment-analysis
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking a reference gene catalogue's sequence-capture efficiency on shotgun metagenomic FASTQ samples, or comparing a new catalogue (e.g. VMGC-90) against an incumbent (e.g. VIRGO) via per-sample mapping rates.

name: metagenomic-read-recruitment-targeted-assembly
description: Use when you need genomic flanking regions around antimicrobial resistance genes (or other target genes) from short-read metagenomic FASTQ data, and full metagenomic de novo assembly is too computationally expensive.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a metagenomic abundance profiler (e.g. BiG-MAP) against known truth: you need simulated shotgun libraries with known gene-cluster abundances to sweep parameter grids (MASH cutoff × Bowtie2 mode) and compute F1.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a taxonomic classifier needs simulated reads with known origin, e.g., ART-generated Illumina/Roche-454 FASTQ sets from genomes whose proteins are excluded from the reference database.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic longitudinal metagenomic reads carrying within-strain SNVs and small InDels with configurable allele-frequency trajectories, to benchmark mutation-detection tools.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking HGT breakpoint detection or local strain reconstruction pipelines against known ground truth, so sensitivity and FDR can be computed from simulated reads at defined coverages.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation-and-alignment
description: Use when benchmarking metagenome binners against curated ground-truth genomes: simulated/sampled per-sample reads must be converted into sorted BAM coverage files and ORF predictions before binning and F1/precision/specificity scoring.

name: metagenomic-read-subsampling
description: Use when a genome in a simulated community is assembled at extreme coverage (e.g. >1000x) and you need to confirm that coverage — not biology — drives the observed misassembled blocks.

name: metagenomic-read-subsampling-replication
description: Use when a user wants to quantify how classification sensitivity and reconstruction completeness degrade with sequencing depth, e.g. testing a pipeline on SRA mock-community reads (FASTQ) at 10/1/0.1% subsampling across replicate trials.

name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-attribution
description: Use when disease-associated genes from MWAS must be assigned to taxa in a shotgun metagenome, e.g., tracing which organisms reads of a specific gene derive from.

name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when you have FASTQ read fractions (mapped/unmapped from read-contig alignment) from a HiFi metagenome assembly and need to know whether low-representation taxa are missing from the assembly.

name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when quality-assuring preprocessed short-read FASTQ metagenomic samples prior to assembly: to classify reads against a reference database, detect contamination, and visualize microbial community composition per sample with Krona charts and a MultiQC report.

name: metagenomic-read-to-protein-alignment
description: Use when quality-filtered (host-filtered, duplicate-filtered, quality-trimmed) shotgun metagenomic FASTQs must be mapped to a microbial protein gene database like UniRef90 to obtain read-to-gene matches for functional profiling.

name: metagenomic-read-type-gating
description: Use when a metagenomic run mixes short-read-only, long-read-only, and paired short+long-read samples, and each sample must be routed to the correct assembly path (MEGAHIT vs SPAdes vs hybridSPAdes) before QUAST-based quality comparison.

name: metagenomic-reference-catalog-retrieval
description: Use when a study needs large, publicly available, redundancy-filtered reference protein catalogs (e.g. as search database input for HH-suite3/BFD or for catalog size/provenance audits) and the input is metagenomic or metatranscriptomic protein sequence space.

name: metagenomic-reference-sequence-comparison
description: Use when candidate transferred segments reconstructed from shotgun metagenomics data must be scored against donor/receptor reference segment sequences to measure local alignment similarity and reconstruction accuracy.

name: metagenomic-sample-metadata-stratification
description: Use when a Qiita-deposited fecal shotgun metagenomics feature table (n=666 paired SPF fecal samples) with metadata fields genotype/study/sex/cohort must be subset (e.g., Sacrifice cohort, per-study) before PERMANOVA or beta-diversity testing.

name: metagenomic-sample-phenotype-classification
description: Use when you have a metagenomic taxonomic profile table (MetaPhlAn merged table or QIIME OTU/BIOM) plus sample metadata with class labels, and the goal is to train a classifier or predict the phenotype of unknown samples.

name: metagenomic-scaffold-sequence-processing
description: Use when input is metagenomic shotgun data or pre-assembled scaftigs with gene predictions (.tab from Prodigal or MetaGeneMark) and the goal is de novo operon prediction without functional or experimental information.

name: metagenomic-scaffolding-misjoin-detection
description: Use when scaffolding metagenomic contigs with paired long-range links and you must decide which contig-pair links are probable interspecies misjoins based on coverage depth and oligonucleotide composition.

name: metagenomic-sequence-clustering-and-retraining

name: method-fabric
description: Routes Microsoft Fabric work (OneLake, Lakehouse, Warehouse, PySpark, Data Factory, Direct Lake, Fabric ML, KQL) with research guardrails. Use when a project uses Fabric.

name: method-fieldwork

Use before decide/plan when you do not yet know what is real, or when the user asks ผู้ใช้ต้องการอะไร / จริงไหม / สัมภาษณ์ / หาข้อมูล / what do users actually want / who is this for / is this real / talk to…

name: method-figure
description: Generate a publication-grade method / architecture / pipeline / workflow figure (a paper or README 'Figure 1') as an AUDITABLE object, not a one-shot prompt. A deterministic JSON blueprint LOCKS the content; an image model (gpt-image-2, baked by the agent via mcp__codex__codex — Codex GPT-5.5 xhigh, sandbox workspace-write) bakes the aesthetic from a labeled-condition render + the project's real identity refs; a cross-model panel (Gemini + Codex) blind-transcribes the result and a script hard-diffs it against the blueprint; the loop regenerates until Gemini AND Codex approve and the diff is e…

name: method-figure
description: Creates and validates publication figures (ggplot2, matplotlib) with a journal-neutral clinical style and manifest. Use when the user wants a Kaplan-Meier, forest, calibration, ROC, or multi-panel figure.

name: method-figure-loop
description: ALIGN for paper figures — draw a method-overview figure as an executable p5.js program that replays its own construction in named stages, exports SVG, and improves through pixel-only cross-model review whose gate is 'explain the method back from the figure alone, and is it worth looking at'. description: ALIGN for paper figures — draw a method-overview figure as an executable p5.js program that replays its own construction in named stages, exports SVG, and improves through pixel-only independent Codex subagent review whose gate is 'explain the method back from the figure alone, and is it worth looking at'. The method sets the relationships the figure must show, the chosen visual identity sets how its marks look, a composition source lends arrangements; the method may be the source's own (意临) or yours in its arrangement (风格迁移). Not for one-shot raster image generation.

name: method-finder
description: Use when someone describes a product problem in their own words and does not know which method fits, or asks which PDT method or canvas to use. Triggers include "welche Methode brauche ich", "ich weiss nicht wo ich anfangen soll", "wie finde ich heraus ob mein Problem echt ist", "wir haben eine Idee, was jetzt", "which canvas should I use", "where do I start with this product". Maps the situation to one of the 85 PDT commands and names the next step.

name: method-framework-design
description: Use when research direction is validated (G1 passed) and the project needs method design, analysis framework, evaluation protocol, or story line — this is Phase 3 and must complete before any code or experiments

name: method-from-expertise
description: Turn what you know into a teachable, reusable method, so you can teach it or build a course or AI training from it consistently.

name: method-gap-detector
description: Detects methodological gaps across study design, analysis, validation, bias control, reproducibility, and implementation readiness within a biomedical research area. Use this skill when a user wants to identify what current studies are still methodologically missing, which weaknesses are most consequential, and what upgrade path would produce a stronger next-step study. Always separate design gaps, analysis gaps, validation gaps, and reproducibility gaps. Never treat technical complexity as methodological rigor.

name: method-gap-research-status
description: Read-only family census that recommends one skill, or none, for a target-specific method-gap research census.

name: method-gauntlet
description: Adversarial review in rotating roles. Each round wears one role (scrutinize, bug-hunter, security, a11y, editor, design-jury, edge-case) so it finds what the other roles structurally cannot, and each round FIRST re-verifies that the previous round's fixes actually landed before hunting new defects. Findings are triaged into fix-now / record-with-price / withdrawn-with-reason. Use to review a diff, a PR, a screen, a spec, or a milestone; when the user says review / loop 2 times / loop 3 times / เปลี่ยน role / adversarial pass / find what is wrong with this.

name: method-genome-build
description: Pins genome build, annotation release, contig naming, and liftover for genomics data. Use when the user mentions GRCh37/38, hg19/hg38, T2T, GENCODE/Ensembl versions, or liftover.

name: method-goal-pursuit
description: Sustain a method-paper goal through evidence-led method iterations, full-scope benchmark experiments, and runnable open-source baseline and SOTA comparisons.

name: method-greenlight
description: The gate ABOVE the plan — build / buy / defer / don't, decided before any code or spec exists. Produces an assumption map (each assumption ranked risk × weakness-of-evidence, with the cheapest test for each), names what is LOST by the simpler option rather than only what is saved, and sets kill criteria BEFORE the build starts. Refuses to approve work whose success cannot be stated as an observable. Use before method-blueprint for anything of real size, or when the user asks ควรทำไหม / ทำเลยไหม / build this? / is X worth building / should we do this at all / do we even need it.

name: method-grill
description: Interviews the user one question at a time to stress-test a study's goal, hypothesis, data, analysis, and journal, recommending answers. Use when the user says grill me.

name: method-groundwork
description: Detects the project's stack and writes .method/config.yml — the file every other method-* skill reads for its commands, mediums, budgets, references, and model tiers. Detects what is knowable from the tree, asks at most six unknowables, and refuses to invent a verify command it cannot find. Runs automatically the first time any other method skill runs in a project with no groundwork laid yet; invoke directly to redo it or to add a reference.

name: method-handoff
description: Creates or resumes a portable continuity record for a data-science task, keeping SAP and real-data gates. Use when work moves to another agent or a later session.

name: method-harvest
description: Session-close capture of reusable METHOD from work just done, drafted as short knowledge-base notes and written only on the user's go. Trigger on a wrap cue ("that's a wrap", "closing this out", "done for today") or an explicit call ("method harvest", "harvest the method", "anything reusable in this session", "what should we keep from this"). Detects up to three candidates, strips them to the concept, states how much evidence stands behind each, and files nothing without approval. Reporting "nothing reusable here" is a correct result. NOT for posts or social content (content-harvest), NOT for…

name: method-human-review
description: Organize human review of an agent-produced artifact when a person requests it, a decision needs their judgment, or authorization is required. Package the exact revision and evidence, capture corrections and the decision, then verify the revised result without treating silence or an agent verdict as approval.

name: method-ideate
description: Generates and ranks grounded research or analysis ideas from repo, literature, or topic context. Use when the user asks for ideas; developing one idea goes to method-brainstorm.

name: method-injection
description: ASP.NET Handler method参数路由接口全面测试 — method枚举发现隐藏API + 注入测试 + IDOR/BOLA + 报错回显

name: method-inventory
description: Comprehensively identify all relevant methods for a task — 50 methods, 60 web searches budget

name: method-journal-select
description: Matches a finished manuscript or abstract to candidate journals by sourced scope fit, indexing, and access policy, returning a ranked target with backups. Use when choosing where to submit.

name: method-ladder
description: Use before any energy, geometry, frequency or spectrum calculation on a molecule or crystal, to choose the level of theory (force field, semi-empirical tight binding, machine-learned potential, DFT or wavefunction) for the question, the system and the time available, and to say what the choice can and cannot show.

name: method-language-detect
description: Detects R, Python, or mixed-language signals in repo files and emits a language handoff. Use when a skill needs language evidence or the user asks the repo's stack.

name: method-launch
description: The pre-push and deploy discipline. Migrations assert their own end state and are additive and re-runnable; production schema is verified BEFORE the push that needs it; the commit body records the why, the measurement, and the rejected alternative; budgets ratchet down only and any raise needs a written reason in the diff. Use when committing, migrating, or deploying.

name: method-lesson
description: Turn something learned in a session (a gap between a request and the kit, an artefact that did not fit, a mistake, a rule the Project Advisor stated) into one dated lesson written at the right place - CLAUDE.md, a skill, a template, the reference design or the kit's CLAUDE.md template - then propagate and journal it (standing rule "Improve the project from every interaction"). Use as soon as a gap is named and the Project Advisor says yes to the fix, or whenever he states a way of working.

name: method-library-content-completeness
description: For goal-based routines that keep the Hamster method/skill/routine content library complete. Verifies the tracking table in the Longform Skills, Methods & Routine Content blueprint is current, adds missing rows, and processes gaps.

name: method-lit-search
description: Routes a literature request to PubMed, full-text evidence mapping, or authoritative web sources. Use when the user broadly asks for papers or evidence.

name: method-lockpick
description: The discipline behind the `security` review role. Reviews a diff, endpoint, migration, or feature by asking who can reach this, who can do it, and what they see when they do — authorization before input validation, because the worst bugs are legitimate requests from the wrong caller. Every finding names the caller, the path, and the data crossed, and is settled against the running system rather than the diff. Use when reviewing anything that touches auth, a server action, an endpoint, a query, a migration, or money.

name: method-logbook
description: The standing ledger of decisions — every idea built, refused-with-price, or queued-with-trigger, in one document so nobody re-derives a dead one. Refuses a silent drop: a considered idea leaves as a priced record or a triggered queue entry, never as silence. Records verdicts from method-greenlight, priced declines from method-blueprint and method-gauntlet, and postmortem outcomes. Use when a decision is made or reversed, when the user asks ทิ้ง / บันทึกไว้ / ทำไปแล้วยัง / what did we decide about X / did we already reject this / add this to the register / why didn't we build Y.

name: method-longlist
description: Generating options worth choosing between — not volume, but N genuinely different approaches from named angles (cheapest, most robust, most reversible, best for the user, and do-nothing, always included), each with what it costs and what it forecloses, then a judge pass that scores them and synthesises from the winner while grafting the best of the runners-up. Use when facing a decision with only one option on the table, or when the user asks มีทางเลือกอะไรบ้าง / คิดหลายๆ แบบ / ทางเลือกอื่น / what are the options / how else could we do this / brainstorm approaches / give me alternatives.

name: method-lookout
description: A threat model scoped to what is actually being built — STRIDE applied to one feature, diff, or milestone, producing a short ranked list of what an attacker would try and what already stops each one. Ends in review tasks and guards, not a document nobody reads. Use before building anything that handles credentials, money, other people's data, file uploads, or external input; or when the user says threat model / attack surface / what could go wrong.

name: method-ltrg
description: Use when a finite-temperature Linearized Tensor Renormalization Group (LTRG) reproduction needs method-level route and tool selection — Trotterized classical tensor network from a quantum lattice model, layer-by-layer boundary contraction with SVD truncation, thermodynamic observables (free energy, internal energy, specific heat, susceptibility).

name: method-marimo
description: Creates, edits, validates, and reviews marimo reactive Python notebooks (UI widgets, PEP 723, export). Use when working on a marimo notebook; Jupyter edits go to method-notebook-edit.

name: method-maturity-assessment
description: Load when a user wants a set of methods, practices or techniques inventoried, classified and assessed for maturity, ending in a scored assessment and an advancement roadmap. Not for choosing an external framework (framework-adoption-assessment) or rating an AI system's autonomy level (ai-autonomy-maturity-classification).

name: method-meta-analysis
description: Pools literature effects with REML/Hartung-Knapp. Use when power or a SAP needs a cited effect-size assumption and sensitivity range.

name: method-mf
description: Use when a mean-field reproduction needs method-level routing — Hartree-Fock / unrestricted Hartree-Fock for lattice fermions, Weiss mean-field decoupling of spin models, self-consistent-field order parameters and phase diagrams.

name: method-mimic
description: Reverse-engineers an existing artefact — a whole site, a single screen, or a design system/component library — into this codebase by measurement rather than eyeball. Runs a scaled version of the five-phase extraction protocol (visual audit, component inventory, layout architecture, tech-stack analysis, documented output), copies real content and real assets verbatim, never copies someone else's brand or licensed imagery, and ends with a mandatory pixel-parity verification against the reference. Use when the request says clone / เลียนแบบ / "make it look like X" / "rebuild this page", or suppli…

name: method-ml-track
description: Adds reproducible ML experiment tracking (data hashes, splits, metrics, SAP links) with MLflow, W&B, DVC, or an offline log. Use when building or reviewing ML experiments.

name: method-model-card
description: Generates a clinical model card: intended use, data, performance with intervals, calibration, fairness, limits. Use when the user asks for a model card.

name: method-model-choice
description: Chooses and justifies the statistical model (regression, mixed/GEE, survival, causal, prediction, Bayesian) after the estimand is set. Use when the user asks which model to fit.

name: method-mps
description: Use when an MPS / matrix-product-state reproduction or calculation needs method-level route and tool selection — ground states, order parameters, correlations, gaps, dynamics, or finite-T of 1D and quasi-1D (narrow-cylinder) Hamiltonians, in either the finite-chain regime (DMRG, TEBD) or the infinite / uniform regime (VUMPS, IDMRG, iTEBD, TDVP). Covers picking the algorithm and routing to the tool.

name: method-notebook-edit
description: Edits existing Jupyter .ipynb notebooks with cell anchors, backups, and metadata-preserving writes. Use when the user asks to patch an existing .ipynb.

name: method-notebook-standards
description: Sets the structure and documentation contract for new or extended marimo, Jupyter, R Markdown, and Quarto notebooks. Use when creating notebook cells or chunks.

name: method-numbers
description: Locks manuscript numbers to an analysis-written registry; a fail-closed gate traces each to its SAP output, script commit, and source hash. Use when reporting or checking results.

name: method-of-moments-polygenic-regression
description: Use when you need per-cell, pathway-level estimates of genetic association from GWAS summary statistics and a normalized single-cell Seurat object, e.g. to compute scPagwas.gPAS.score for trait-relevant cell identification.

name: method-omics-qc
description: Runs sequencing and omics QA: FASTQ, BAM/CRAM, VCF, count matrices, methylation arrays, sample swaps, batch confounding. Use when omics data needs QC before analysis.

name: method-optimize
description: Runs bounded, metric-scored experiment loops to improve a model, prompt, or pipeline without touching the test set. Use when a scored metric must improve; broken runs go to method-debug.

name: method-orchestrator
description: Orchestrator skill for the Method / System / Experimental Setup section - delegates writing to the method subagent (this file is the rulebook the subagent loads at startup), routes open questions to paper-researcher and reviews to paper-reviewer1/2; the main conversation never writes prose itself. Use this skill whenever the user is writing the Method, System, Experimental Setup, Apparatus, or Implementation section of a paper — the chapter that describes the technical system or platform built before running the user study. Triggers include "Method", "Experimental Setup", "System", "実装", "手法"…

name: method-parameterized-spectra-transformation
description: Use when a 1H-NMR spectra DataFrame (columns = chemical shifts in ppm, rows = samples) shows baseline distortions from incomplete relaxation, pulse sequence imperfections, magnetic field inhomogeneities, solvent effects, phase errors, or macromolecules.

name: method-peps
description: Use when a PEPS, iPEPS, CTMRG, 2D tensor-network, environment dimension, or classical partition-function reproduction needs method-level route and tool selection.

name: method-performance-comparison-tabulation
description: Use when a newly proposed computational method's identification performance must be quantified against established baselines under controlled perturbations like added noise or spurious-correlation confounders.

name: method-phenotype
description: Validates a computable phenotype against chart review: 2x2 table, PPV, NPV, sensitivity, specificity, Wilson intervals. Use when checking a phenotype or code list.

name: method-picker
description: Help a SYSEN 5300 student choose a defensible method — which distribution, which control chart, which capability index, which test, regression vs. DOE vs. RSM — by interrogating the question and the data first, then naming the trade-offs. Invoked as /methodpick. Never runs the analysis, designs the study, or writes the code.

name: method-plan
description: Creates the durable plan for data-science work: an implementation plan or, for studies, a statistical analysis plan (SAP). Use when the user asks to plan work or write a SAP.

name: method-pm-audit
description: Playbook for auditing PM-health across 15 dimensions (Discovery, Strategy, Prioritization, Roadmap, Specs, Metrics, Launch, Measure, Comms, Decisions, Pricing, Competitive, Feedback, AI-PM, Governance) and producing a structured report. The brain behind pm-auditor.

name: method-polisher

Use this skill whenever the user wants to improve, restructure, evaluate, or rewrite the Method (or Methods, Methodology) section of a research paper. Triggers include: "polish my methods section", "is my methodology clear enough", "help me describe my procedure", "my methods section is too vague", or uploading a paper and asking to improve the methodology description. Also trigger when the user asks whether their method section has enough detail for replication.

name: method-polyopt
description: Use when a noncommutative polynomial optimization reproduction needs method-level route and tool selection — certified lower bounds on ground-state energy via the moment-SOS / SOHS (NPA-style) hierarchy solved as a semidefinite program, Bell-inequality maximum quantum violation, or state-polynomial / tracial optimization. Triggers include polynomial optimization, SOS / SOHS relaxation, moment-SOS hierarchy, NPA hierarchy, certified energy lower bound, Bell inequality, semidefinite relaxation, NCTSSoS.

name: method-power
description: Calculates sample size and power for clinical, survival, cluster, and prediction-model studies, with a script, sweep, and SAP text. Use when the user asks for power or sample size.

name: method-ppt
description: 根据用户的论文组会和课程汇报偏好，制作、修改可编辑PPT， 并编写与最终页序对应的口播稿。适用于论文分享、课程汇报、技术方案讲解， 或用户要求“按之前的汇报风格”“按我的习惯做PPT”时。 重点是原文依据、方法叙事、公式各项的作用、算法步骤与局部批注修改； 内容、页数、版式和深度随本次任务调整。单独的概念提问不自动触发文件修改。

name: method-pr
description: Commits, pushes, and opens or updates a pull request with a value-first body, keeping data and PHI out. Use when the user asks to ship or open a PR.

name: method-prd
description: PRD with ruthless MVP scope and testable acceptance criteria. Use when writing a product requirements document.

name: method-precedent
description: Search for published papers that justify a specific methodological decision. Returns precedents diversified across empirical domains, with top papers read in full via PDF.

name: method-prereg
description: Generates preregistration and registry content for OSF, ClinicalTrials.gov, PROSPERO, or a study protocol. Use when the user asks to preregister or register a study.

name: method-presubmit
description: Runs the final gate on a manuscript, abstract, cover letter, or grant: section discipline, voice, and anti-slop passes. Use when a draft is about to go to co-authors.

name: method-problem-crossing
description: Build method×problem cross-reference matrix showing which methods have been applied to which problems.

name: method-problem-matrix
description: Cross method×problem matrix, find unexplored intersections where known methods have not been applied to known problems.

name: method-pubmed
description: Searches PubMed/MEDLINE via E-utilities with MeSH-aware queries into a PMID and abstract CSV. Use when the user explicitly wants PubMed or PMIDs; broad asks go to method-lit-search.

name: method-puppeteer
description: Security for features that call a model — prompt injection from fetched or user-supplied content, model output treated as data rather than markup or instructions, the authority a tool call carries, and spend as an attack surface. Built on one rule: a model's output is untrusted input, and the place it lands decides what it can do. Use when building or reviewing anything that prompts a model, renders model output, gives a model tools, or ingests retrieved content.

name: method-qcs
description: Use when a quantum circuit simulation, VQE, TensorCircuit-NG, JAX backend, contraction path, statevector, MPS circuit, gradient, or circuit-performance reproduction needs method-level route and tool selection.

name: method-qmc

Triggers include "QMC", "SSE", "stochastic series expansion", "finite-temperature susceptibility", "sign problem", "AFQMC", "CPMC", "constrained path", "Hubbard ground state by Monte Carlo", "DMC", "diffusion Monte Carlo…

name: method-question
description: Turns one chosen biomedical study idea into PICO, FINER, a hypothesis, and PubMed-query YAML. Use when the user wants PICO/FINER framing; open design exploration goes to method-brainstorm.

name: method-r
description: Routes R work: analysis design, tidyverse, event-study DiD, packages, testthat, CRAN, profiling, targets. Use when a project is R-first or the user needs R help; diffs and PRs go to method-review.

name: method-r-trace-analyzer
description: Analyzes Oracle extended SQL trace files using Method R tools (mrskew, mrcrop, mrkey, mrwhen, mr1011) and Cary Millsap's performance methodology. Use when profiling response times, diagnosing wait events and resource consumption (CPU, LIO, PIO), scoping trace files into user experiences, identifying bottlenecks, or providing SQL tuning recommendations.

name: method-ranking-table-generation
description: Use when a paper's claim of one method outperforming baselines must be reproduced: multiple cell-type identification methods are run on identical data and ranked by accuracy and F1-score in a comparison table.

name: method-reading
description: Read a living doc as a method surface and report objective, current state, ontology, control, evidence, value, and optional risk, solution-space, and convergence-advice sidecars with grounding.

name: method-reconstruction
description: Reverse-engineer a computer-science / machine-learning / mathematics paper into a runnable, traceable Python codebase when the authors released no code — the core of the toolkit. Use when the user says "the authors gave no code", "turn this paper into Python", "reconstruct this architecture/algorithm/loss from the paper", "reverse engineer this ML method so we can validate it", or when a claim needs code before it can be tested. Extracts the model ARCHITECTURE, the MATHEMATICS (losses, update rules, equations), the HYPERPARAMETERS, and the ALGORITHM/procedure, and emits a structured Python pr…

name: method-red-team
description: Gate-time adversarial review of strategy or design artifacts. Use before G1, G2 and G3.

name: method-refinement
description: Compile the approved ResearchOS method intent and current root-owned iteration decision into a versioned, implementation-ready method specification with stable module contracts, training/inference flows, config and ablation interfaces, failure modes, intent/spec fingerprints, an explicit delta ledger, and a pre-implementation scope-drift gate. Use when `research-execution` dispatches initial method engineering before implementation, when an approved minor refinement follows diagnosis or attribution, or when a stale method specification must be rebuilt after an authorized plan or protocol chan…

name: method-relations
description: Screens methods into candidate groups, decides which of six relations holds inside one group, and rewrites the affected methods under that decision. Use for a consolidate job carrying a frozen method-relations-input.json and one named action - screen, decide or build.

name: method-release-notes
description: Summarizes recent methodsmith plugin releases from release metadata. Use when the user asks what changed in the plugin or whether a skill shipped.

name: method-replayer
description: Create interactive replay notebooks that unwrap a Python entrypoint, method, or evaluation pipeline into a user-runnable, inspection-first notebook with explicit assumptions, source-code links, and stepwise checkpoints. Use when Codex should help an experienced user reproduce, audit, or trace a result manually in Jupyter rather than running the whole workflow itself, especially for ML training and evaluation pipelines, result mismatches, merge or reconstruction flows, or codepath debugging.

name: method-repo-api-discovery
description: 在陌生或并行变化的代码库中需要调用、修改或审查内部 API，且类名、函数名、参数签名、返回结构、生命周期或 callsite 不确定时使用。通过定义面、类型/注释和完整调用点一次查证替代 ImportError、TypeError 和猜参数式试错；适用于代码审计、接入、重构和签名变更。已明确掌握当前版本 API 契约的简单调用无需加载。

name: method-report-bug
description: Collects a reproducible methodsmith plugin bug report and files or drafts a GitHub issue. Use when the user wants to report a plugin bug.

name: method-resolve-feedback
description: Resolves review feedback on analysis or code PRs, methodology comments included: triages, fixes, validates, replies. Use when the user asks to address PR comments.

name: method-review
description: Review code for method-level clarity by applying decomposition, conditional structure, boolean simplification, and unnecessary-machinery principles. Use when the user asks to simplify methods, clean up conditionals, flatten logic, reduce complexity, or improve how individual methods are expressed.

name: method-review
description: Review code for method-level clarity by applying reuse, decomposition, conditional structure, boolean simplification, and unnecessary-machinery principles. Use when the user asks to simplify or clean up code or a diff, clean up conditionals, flatten logic, reduce complexity, or improve how individual functions are expressed. For whether the overall design fits the problem, use structural-review.

name: method-review
description: Reviews data-science code changes with statistical, methods, PHI, and engineering personas and confidence-gated findings. Use when the user asks for code or PR review.

name: method-review
description: Focus areas: `routing`, `tokens`, `delegation`, `tools`, `parallelism`, `full`

name: method-root-cause
description: 面对回归、性能骤降、缓存异常、协议错误、行为变化或“最近改了什么导致问题”这类根因分析任务时使用。要求先冻结真实 baseline、建立可证伪假设、用单变量实验区分数据/协议/runtime/模型/验证方式，再做最小修复；适用于避免看到异常就 patch 或多变量一起修改造成伪归因。根因和修复已由直接证据明确时无需加载。

name: method-router

allowed_tools: list_workflows, run_status, ask, risk_exposure, risk_register_check, risk_report, risk_candidates, coverage_report

name: metis-risk-manager-quantitative

allowed_tools: list_workflows, run_status, ask, risk_register_check, risk_report, risk_categories, risk_exposure

name: metis-risk-manager-release-risk

name: minder:mem:capture-candidate

name: minder:mem:check-decision

name: minder:mem:content

Publishing stays a manual owner act — the bright line. Additive + idempotent + resumable.

name: minder:mem:lint

Confidence tier routing (silent/noted/reviewed/surfaced/hidden) via rule-floor × LLM-verdict. Dedup = content-merging (not destructive). Cross-skill lock awareness symmetric. Best-effort, idempotent, rollback via git.

name: minder:mem:maintain

name: minder:mem:role:add

The owner never sees frontmatter, never picks a cadence, never learns what a write-prefix is. Nothing is declared done until the config validates, every credential has been proven…

Holds `.roles.lock` while writing, so an edit can never land in the middle of a running tick. Pausing and resuming a role is this same skill.

When there are no roles yet, says so and offers to create one.

name: minder:mem:roles

The guard check runs after every dispatch whatever happened (success, error, timeout, crash), then one run line lands in that role's log.jsonl, then that role's work is committed before the next one starts — named paths only, `[scheduled]` in the subject, never `git add -A`, never a leaked credential. name: mindset-false-growth-check
description: 做什么：审计自称成长型的做法是否只是口头化、只夸努力、见效即停，或努力在为"证明自己"服务，给一个最先改的替换动作。 何时激活：个人、家长、学校或团队自认为已是成长型或在推行，但行为、结果或气氛没变。 触发信号："我早就是成长型思维了，可还是一失败就崩""我们一直夸孩子努力，但没用""公司天天讲成长型文化，可谁犯错谁倒霉""我很努力，但其实是怕被看不起""用了那些方法见效后就又打回原形""我是不是假成长型"。 不触发 → 去哪：还没识别自己在哪个时刻出问题 → mindset-reaction-diagnosis；只想改一句具体的表扬或批评 → mindset-process-praise；想针对某个触发点定改变计划 → mindset-trigger-reframe；用来指责别人"你这是假成长型" → 不配合，改为讨论具体行为；职业倦怠、过劳伴身体症状 → psyche。 边界：躯体症状或失眠≥2 周先转 psyche；资源、考核、歧视等结构问题不归因到心态；不承诺换做法就见效。

Use when you can't get absorbed in important work, find yourself distracted and scattered, feel chronically bored or chronically anxious in your work, want to design conditions for deep work, or used to experience flow and have lost it. Triggers: 'flow', 'deep work', 'I can't focus', 'I'm always distracted', 'I want to get absorbed in my work', 'I feel bored at work', 'I used to experience flow and I don't anymore', 'optimal experience', 'getting in the zone'.

Use when you're treating failure as evidence about your identity, avoiding challenges because of what failure would mean, comparing yourself to others in a way that deflates rather than inspires, or struggling to persist in areas where you're not naturally good. Triggers: 'growth mindset', 'I hate not being good at things', 'failure feels personal', 'I avoid things I might fail at', 'I feel stupid when I struggle', 'fixed mindset', 'talent vs. effort'.
